comparator.sourceNotes: The current RSM curriculum establishes a fixed 60-EC first year, a fixed 60-EC second year and a flexible 60-EC third year. This coherent pathway preserves the first 30 EC of year 3 as a 15-EC minor plus 15 EC of open elective space, includes the 13-EC compulsory third-year core, and instantiates the 17-EC Navigating Stakeholders in Global Business track. That track is the broadest continuation of the programme's general international-business identity; AI and Accounting & Finance are more specialised alternatives. The route choice is independent of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: International business, management & entrepreneurship
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible international-business programme combining strategy, entrepreneurship, marketing, leadership and organisational behaviour with accounting, finance, economics, research, data, technology, law and global governance.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines international business and management with entrepreneurship, economics, finance, marketing, data, law and leadership; the label therefore names its broad business composition.
progression: Business, economics, data and research foundations precede advanced strategy, law, leadership, econometrics and market research. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.
traceOverrides: examines managerial and organisational implications of AI and technological change within a broad international-business curriculum
introduces machine-learning models for evidence-based analysis within the programme's data and technology strand
develops microeconomic and behavioural analysis of consumer and firm decisions

alternatives.label: Business, AI & digital transformation
alternatives.concept: An international-business route organised around artificial intelligence, data and digital transformation, combining programming, machine learning and deep learning with strategy, organisations, marketing, finance and responsible AI.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum retains a substantial business core while adding a sequenced programming, mathematics, data, algorithms and AI strand, so the label names both business and AI.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces much of the general economics, law, communication and leadership mix with programming, mathematics, algorithms, databases, machine learning, deep learning and AI ethics.
progression: Business, programming, data, research and mathematical foundations precede advanced strategy, algorithms, machine learning, deep learning, international business and market research. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, probability and deep learning; programming precedes algorithms. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Finance, accounting & global business
alternatives.concept: A global-business route centred on accounting, finance and analytical decision-making, combining corporate finance, banking, economics and econometrics with probability, data science, programming, databases, machine learning and international governance.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around finance and accounting but also contains economics, quantitative analysis, strategy and international governance, so the label includes global business.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match and the AI route, this curriculum gives greater weight to finance, banking, accounting, economics, econometrics, probability and behavioural decision-making while retaining an international-business foundation.
progression: Business, economics, programming, data, research and mathematical foundations precede public economics, international business, probability, machine learning, econometrics, behavioural economics and finance. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra and probability; Business Foundations precedes Money, Banking & Finance and International Business & Governance. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

candidates.label: Accounting and Finance for International Business

routeSelection.basis: The generic IBA target requires one current third-year track. Navigating Stakeholders in Global Business most directly continues the programme's broad international-business and management identity, whereas AI for a Connected World and Accounting & Finance for International Business are more specialised. It is also the first current track in the official curriculum; the choice is independent of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Two additional formal, generator-backed directions are coherent and feasible after the closest match: AI for a Connected World and Accounting & Finance for International Business. Both produce curricula that are substantively distinct and exceed the 30-EC pairwise floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

blocks: Both develop personal leadership and professional growth within organisational settings.
Leadership Communication addresses ethical influence and leadership practice, a substantial part of responsible business leadership.
Both address managing diversity and inclusion in workforces and organisational settings.
Both provide research design, quantitative methods and statistical analysis for business questions; the comparator component is more extensive.
Market Research applies research design, data collection and analysis to a business problem.
Econometrics directly covers regression-based quantitative analysis central to the methods master classes.
Decision-making in AI addresses formal planning, optimisation and resource allocation under constraints.
Both develop practical data handling, modelling and analysis skills, although UCR uses broader data-science tools rather than spreadsheet modelling alone.
Both examine how technology changes organisations and managerial decisions; the UCR course focuses specifically on AI-era business.
Database Management Systems provides a specific information-management foundation through organisational data structures and SQL.
Both examine how international businesses navigate institutions, governance and external stakeholders.

notes.text: RSM's IBA programme provides a dense compulsory sequence across international business functions, including operations, supply chains, human-resource management, management accounting and business simulation, plus a formal third-year track and bachelor project. UCR can build coherent international-business, AI and finance programmes, but it does not reproduce the same complete functional sequence or formal track/project structure.
